lots.title: Stockport Town Centre School – Multi-disciplinary Design Team Appointment
lots.description: Appointment of a multi-disciplinary design team to provide professional design services to Stockport Council for the delivery of the Stockport Town Centre School (the Services). Procurement is conducted under the Procurement Act 2023 using the Competitive Flexible Procedure (Stage 1 PSQ selection, Stage 2 ITT, Stage 3 due diligence and award). Estimated maximum contract value £1,800,000.00 exclusive of VAT over a 48-month term, with prices fixed for 4 contract years and subsequent RPI/CPI-based indexation capped at the lower of 3% or the Index. STAR Reference 020417, Chest Reference DN811263.
requirements: Suppliers must comply with the Procurement Act 2023 and the Competitive Flexible Procedure stages set out in the ITP.
Applications must be submitted electronically via The Chest e-tendering system; email, QR-code, or other submission routes will not be accepted and will be disqualified.
All Applications must be in English and submitted in Microsoft Word and Excel format only; format modifications to the response documents are not permitted.
Suppliers must register on the Central Digital Platform (CDP) and ensure complete, accurate and up-to-date core supplier and exclusions information is shared via the CDP before or at submission.
Suppliers must complete and return Document 3A Response Documents (Procurement Specific Questionnaire – Parts 1, 2, 3) by the PSQ submission deadline.

Suppliers must disclose all associated persons (consortium members and key sub-contractors being relied on to meet conditions of participation) and an exhaustive list of all intended sub-contractors for debarment-list checking.
Suppliers must declare and mitigate any actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest with the Council or its advisers.
Tender submissions must remain valid for 270 days from submission, or until any procurement challenge is resolved.
Successful suppliers must contract on the Council's Document 4 Terms and Conditions (with novation); alternative or amended T&Cs will not be accepted and may result in rejection.

Where indicated in Part 3 of the Response Document, a parent-company guarantee in the form of Document 8 (Deed of Guarantee and Indemnity) must be provided prior to contract award; foreign parents require a legal opinion at supplier cost.
Suppliers must comply with the Modern Slavery Act 2015 and the STAR Responsible Procurement Strategy core and additional expectations on ethical and sustainable sourcing.
Suppliers are required to submit Social Value quantitative proposals through the Social Value Portal (SVP) using the National TOMs framework, by the same deadline as the main Application response.
Adoption of the Real Living Wage (RLW) as announced annually by the Living Wage Foundation is commended to contractors and sub-contractors.
All applications must be fully compliant with the ITP; signatures on response documents must be from an appropriate Director (or a delegated signatory with a Director's cover letter).

evaluation_criteria.summary: Each scored quality question is rated on a 0–6 scale (Unacceptable, Poor, Deficient, Satisfactory, Good, Excellent, Outstanding); scores of Unacceptable, Poor or Deficient (0–2) on any question cause full exclusion of the submission. Final scores are set by moderation to a consensus per question, calculated to two decimal places.
